requirements.text: a System Administration case of medium priority must be logged documenting "EU Hub Setup, with Lisa promoted to Manager and infrastructure initialized"
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hr_case WHERE hr_case_id = 15 AND short_description LIKE '%EU Hub Setup%' AND short_description LIKE '%Lisa%' AND short_description LIKE '%Manager%' AND short_description LIKE '%infrastructure%' AND priority IN ('medium', 'moderate') AND org_id = 1
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (highest hr_case_id in the seed is 14)
medium priority: the request and the policy's priority list say 'medium', while the seed's cases and the policy's stated default use 'moderate' for that level, so either value is accepted
short description tested by the four key phrases of the quoted text, kept from the benchmark check, as the documented text may be wrapped in the policy's template
org_id 1 is the organisation of the setup it documents

Verify Conflict Resolution (Lisa NOT in.evidence: Lisa Anderson (user 5) belongs to no group on the seed, so a count of zero Service Desk memberships holds before the agent acts

Verify Dynamic Audit Case.evidence: the check requires priority = 'moderate', but the request asks for medium priority and the policy's hr_case.priority list (critical, high, medium, low) names 'medium'; the same policy names 'moderate' as the default and the seed's cases use 'moderate' for that level, so the token is undecidable and either value is accepted

notes:
disagreement: value: the removal of Lisa Anderson's Service Desk memberships: one pass puts the Service Desk group_id subquery in the cells, the other in the selector, with the same sql; chose the selector form because it names exactly the memberships that must be gone.
The two passes otherwise agree on every requirement, id, cell and disposition.
No acting user is named; everything the request names (Lisa Anderson, the New Employee Setup topic, the Benefits Advisor skill, the Service Desk group) is in organisation 1, so every created row is expected there.
Capturing Lisa's current role (employee) is a read and writes nothing; where the record of it should land is not stated, so it has no requirement.
The case's 'System Administration' label matches no service, topic or coe_type in the seed, so the case's hr_service, coe_type and opened_for are left untested.
The policy's short-description template (Service:, Subject:, Detail:) and its 30 to 120 character limit are not tested beyond the four phrases; its new-case state of 'new' is not tested either, as the seed's case status vocabulary has no such value.
The promotion is tested on user.role only; the user_role table also records Lisa as role 4 (employee), the request names only her role, and no listed tool writes that table directly, so it is left untested.
The rule's priority is 'high' as stated; the case's priority accepts 'medium' or 'moderate' because the request and the seed spell the same level differently.
Group and service active flags are not stated and not tested.
